I've been picking up some literature about science (especially philosophy of science) lately, and thought I'd give a few recommendations.

The scientific attitude by Lee Mcintyre.

A wonderful book on how to tell science from non-science, why science has a privileged claim on epistemic truth, all boiling down to cultural values shared by scientists. Also quite an interesting take on the demarcation problem and suggestions for how to improve science and scientific communication in general. A light and lucid read, highly recommended.

Down to Earth by Bruno Latour

A dense and heavy philosophical/sociological take on the current political climate and its interplay with science and facts. Extremely insightful and topical, but this small book is quite a lot to digest. Luckily the author has a good sense of humor. Don't be alarmed if the first chapter seems too much, it gets lighter from chapter two onwards.

The death of expertise by Tom Nichols

Light, funny, slightly depressing. Tom Nichols unpacks the layperson's lack of trust and respect for experts and expertise. He does a wonderful job of showing how multi-faceted this issue is, and how all these mechanisms tend to feed into each other. Sadly, he seems content only with identifying and explaining the issues at hand, with very little in the way of advice. It is however an excellent read that will teach you to spot these mechanism in action in the real world.

What are your recommendations? Anything interesting you've read lately?
